This intermediate compound, in turn, is shown to have a target relationship with SF-188. The integrated evidence suggests a potential pathway where Canrenoic acid influences the function of the neuronal acetylcholine receptor, which is then modulated by the 1,4,7-trihydroxy-2-methoxy-6-methylanthracene-9,10-dione. This chain of interactions implies that Canrenoic acid may act as a modulator of SF-188 through its interaction with the acetylcholine receptor subunit alpha-3. The mechanism is supported by the observed scores and the direct target relationships, though the exact functional role of the intermediate compound remains to be elucidated.
